acceptance.given: A repository-owned skill-package replay receives a target path that resolves outside the repository or otherwise violates target legality before validator execution.

oracle.expected: The replay rejects the target before target-dependent validation or processing begins.
forbidden: Accepting or processing an illegal target as valid.
oracle.observable: The selected replay test observes a nonzero result with the target-legality rejection and no validator success receipt.

acceptance.then: The illegal target is rejected and processing remains closed.
acceptance.when: When the resolved target violates legality requirements.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Exercise validate-package with an escaping or illegal target and require rejection before validator execution.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Extend the repository-owned package replay boundary, under ADR-0058, so illegal resolved targets are rejected fail-closed before validation can process them.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or receipt-schema migration; rollback restores only the Toolchain replay legality check and its unit coverage.

slice_hint.state_transition: A target resolution attempt identifying an illegal target transitions to a rejected, non-processing outcome.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selected Toolchain unit test proves that an illegal target returns nonzero before validator success can occur.

acceptance.given: A replay result and its recorded current-snapshot identity exist, and a result-determining input changes without an approved explanation.

oracle.expected: The replay result is marked stale or the replay path refuses to proceed.
forbidden: An unexplained result-determining input drift is ignored.
The result is treated as current and valid despite unexplained result-determining input drift.
Replay continues as successful without a stale designation or fail-closed outcome.
oracle.observable: The current-router test reports the changed snapshot identity as invalidating the prior observation and routes the result to rerun or fail-closed handling.

acceptance.then: The result is stale or the replay path has failed closed.
acceptance.when: When unexplained drift occurs in an input that determines the result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the current-router stale-observation selector against a changed current-snapshot identity and observe the pre-change failure that wrongly leaves the result reusable or current.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Under ADR-0058, make the Toolchain current-router invalidate a replay observation when an unexplained result-determining current-snapshot identity differs, routing it as stale or fail-closed rather than reusable success.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted-state or schema compatibility change; rollback removes only the current-snapshot drift invalidation behavior and its unit assertion.

slice_hint.state_transition: A replay result with unexplained result-determining input drift transitions from reusable/current to stale or a fail-closed replay route.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selected Toolchain unit test proves that a changed result-determining snapshot identity cannot leave the replay result reusable or successful.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain external-process descriptor has an applicable finite output bound and the launched process emits output.

oracle.expected: The executor records output at or below the applicable bound or terminates the bounded execution unsuccessfully when the bound is exhausted.
forbidden: An external process exceeds its output bound.
An external process produces unbounded output.
oracle.observable: The immutable process receipt and bounded stdout/stderr artifacts record the configured output limit, observed bounded output, and an unsuccessful terminal classification when the limit is exhausted.

acceptance.then: The external process has produced output within its applicable output bound.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the runtime-stage selector with a process that attempts to emit beyond its declared finite output bound and require a bounded unsuccessful receipt rather than unbounded capture or success.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Under ADR-0058, add finite output-bound enforcement and receipt facts to the Toolchain external-process executor; output-budget exhaustion must terminate deterministically as unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Receipt changes are additive and preserve existing fields; rollback removes only the output-bound fields and enforcement while retaining prior receipt compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: An external process with an applicable output bound transitions to a bounded terminal receipt; output-budget exhaustion transitions to unsuccessful.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selected runtime test proves that a process attempting excess output cannot produce unbounded artifacts or a successful terminal result.

acceptance.given: The repository-owned Toolchain package replay evaluates an independently invalid package case.

oracle.expected: The invalid-package case has a rejected-success, nonzero outcome.
forbidden: Success is accepted for an invalid-package case.
oracle.observable: The replay test observes that the invalid package cannot produce a successful validation receipt, including when a validator would otherwise return success.

acceptance.when: When an invalid-package case is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate an invalid package with an always-success validator and require rejection of the otherwise green result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Under ADR-0058, preserve the Toolchain replay discriminator so an invalid package cannot obtain success merely because its validator exits zero.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or schema change; rollback restores only the repository-owned invalid-package success gate and its unit coverage.

slice_hint.state_transition: An invalid-package case under evaluation transitions to rejected success and cannot contribute a successful replay result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selected Toolchain unit test proves that an invalid package, including one paired with an always-success validator, cannot produce an accepted success result.
